title: How does an escalator work?
timing_note: Expanded from the initial 30-second target to explain the mechanism in a conversation. All times are provisional edit estimates; use the finished voices at normal generation rate and 1x playback to set final timing.

Sol.performance: Exaggerated cartoon student; mouthless, with intentional morphs of the original two navy eye shapes, anticipation, squash/stretch, fast takes, and held reactions.

Narrator.performance: Off-screen; conversational and engaged, responding directly to Sol.

staging: One upward-running mall escalator, lower floor on screen left and upper landing on screen right. The rising steps always travel left to right; the hidden return run travels right to left. Warm painted mall lighting. One step has an orange editorial highlight so the viewer can track it. Sol rides that step at the opening, then stays on the upper landing throughout the explanation. Close-ups of other steps do not inherit the orange highlight.
production_notes: This is a review script and clip plan, not a generation request or a timed production edit.
Each clip has a separate first-frame composition, action, and last-frame composition. First and last frames describe visible states.

Use controlled painted diagrams / Remotion animation for the chains, tracks, step orientation, arrows, highlights, and labels. Base step and track geometry on the manufacturer reference. Keep the steps rigid; neighboring steps change relative height, and steps rotate around the return path.
Treat the cutaway as an editorial diagram. Cut to it already visible; no physical panel removal or machinery transforming around Sol.
The overview illustrates the route and does not promise real escalator transit speed. Preserve the orange step's route between the overview views; mechanism close-ups show other steps.
Keep all text, wheel colors, and the orange tracking highlight editable. The finished art must not bake in technical labels.
Edit durations differ by clip. Check provider durations only when generation is requested; longer diagram scenes can be animated directly in Remotion.
The narrator audio text is in narration.txt; Sol's audio text is in sol-dialogue.txt. Those files contain only spoken words. Speaker labels and scene directions remain in script.txt and this plan.

Cartoon direction updated Nov. 13, 2026: morph the existing two navy eye shapes intentionally, preserve their home placement and color, and keep the recognizable layered flame design. Each visible character clip specifies first/last expression states and cue-based acting beats.

Composition percentages are planning guides within the vertical frame. Test the approved still at phone size before generation; keep eye shapes and important mechanism contacts clear of the reserved caption strip.
Use matching painted first/end expression art for the character clips. Strong cartoon acting is requested; motion accents do not change mechanical geometry or the already-reviewed dialogue.

clips.setting_and_framing: Medium full shot on the near side of the upper landing. Camera at the height of Sol's cream face, approximately 30 degrees toward the front from a pure side view, so the tread depth and both of Sol's eyes are visible. Sol starts slightly left of center and exits toward screen right.
clips.first_frame: Sol is fully visible on the orange-highlighted step just before the stationary floor, body centered at x=42% and feet at y=74%. His two eyes are the original neutral navy ovals. His body is upright in three-quarter view, angled toward the exit on screen right; his gaze points ahead to the landing. One stubby arm rests on the handrail.
clips.action: Sol steps right onto the landing. As the highlighted tread disappears, his eyes snap back toward it before his flame body turns. On 'disappear,' both eyes pop into round surprised shapes and his body stretches upward for a brief double-take. His flame tip trails the turn, overshoots, and settles. As he finishes 'floor,' he leans back toward the exit edge from his fixed floor position and settles into an asymmetrical questioning eye shape.

dialogue.speaker: Sol
dialogue.text: Wait, where do these steps go when they disappear into the floor?

clips.last_frame: Sol stands fully on the stationary upper floor, centered around x=66%, with both feet at y=74%. He holds a 15-degree down-left lean. His eye nearer the exit is a tall oval, and the other is shorter and flatter; both stay navy and within the cream face. The orange step is hidden beneath the exit plate, and the following unhighlighted tread remains visible below-left.
clips.next_cut: Hard cut wider to the flat side cutaway in clip 02. Preserve Sol's questioning expression, feet on the upper landing, down-left gaze, and the orange step's just-hidden position.
clips.planned_method: Generate or animate the painted Sol-and-landing scene with explicit expression endpoint art. Control tread travel and the orange highlight separately; add smear/pop accents in the edit.

Both feet planted on the landing, body tilted about 15 degrees toward the mystery; one stubby arm hovers toward the exit, flame tip finishes its delayed settle.

clips.action: As Sol says 'the step I just rode,' he points his stubby arm down-left and follows the orange step with his face. On 'comes back around,' his eyes round in recognition as the step reappears at the entrance. On 'Exactly,' his eyes morph into happy upward-arched crescents; he compresses into a small anticipation squash, makes one springy bounce on the stationary floor, and lands in a relaxed, proud pose. His flame tip finishes a delayed wobble after his feet settle.

dialogue.speaker: Sol
dialogue.text: So the step I just rode comes back around for the next person?

His layered flame body has returned to its compact resting proportions. The original orange-highlighted step is back at the lower entrance, ready for another rider. Both Sol and the returned step remain visible in the gently tighter ending crop.

direction_note: Push the painted 2D staging and acting as far into cartoon performance as possible. Sol's two existing dark eye shapes intentionally morph to express thoughts; his mouthless layered flame design stays recognizable. Dialogue and the provisional 43-second edit remain unchanged.

composition_rules.coordinates: Percentages refer to the 9:16 picture, with x measured from the left and y from the top. They are layout guides for stills, not exact animation coordinates.
composition_rules.captions: Reserve x=10–84%, y=83–92% for editable captions. Keep all eyes, tracked step positions, guide-wheel contacts, and important mechanism connections above y=79%.
composition_rules.background: Simplified rounded mall architecture in soft cream and muted teal, broad painted shadows, warm orange accents. Reduce background contrast around Sol's face and each mechanism detail. Keep the texture visibly painted.
composition_rules.continuity: Stay on the near side of the escalator. The rising run goes lower-left to upper-right; the hidden return goes back toward lower-left. Sol remains physically on the upper landing after clip 01. Camera changes are cuts with their new angle stated explicitly.
composition_rules.performance: Use exaggerated anticipation, squash/stretch, fast eye changes, whole-body takes, flame-tip follow-through, and short held poses. Expressions carry the performance without a mouth.
composition_rules.mechanical_readability: Use oversized, simplified diagram details and cartoon attention effects. The drive chain remains connected, the step bodies remain rigid, and supporting wheels stay on their assigned guide paths.

eye_shapes.neutral: The two original navy vertical ovals at their original home positions on the cream face; no separate pupils.
eye_shapes.surprise: Both ovals become large round navy shapes, roughly one and a half times their neutral width, still separated and contained within the cream face.
eye_shapes.questioning: The eye nearer the gaze target is a tall oval; the other eye is shorter and flatter. Body lean establishes the gaze direction.
eye_shapes.focus: Both eyes compress into short horizontal navy shapes for a held scrutinizing look.
eye_shapes.tracking: The original ovals lean and compress toward the moving object's side, staying near their home positions; body rotation follows the eye change.
eye_shapes.delight: Two thick upward-arched navy crescents, like closed smiling eyes. These are the existing eyes changing shape, not added eyebrows.
